emails.objection: The draft could still say something about the offer that the reader would not approve under their own name.
must_not_say: Do not imply that a campaign or draft is already waiting in the account.

emails.call_to_action: Sign in to your existing MarketingOS workspace, register the brand, add the real material for one offer, and request one launch or onboarding email.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether a draft grounded in the supplied offer material is worth reviewing further for this campaign.
emails.next_step_value: The workspace lets the reader register the brand, add real source material, and request the first email rather than committing to a full sequence.

emails.job: Get the tester to inspect the factual basis and simulated-reader feedback for the generated draft before deciding what to keep or rewrite.
emails.single_idea: The useful review is not a score taken on faith: the reader can inspect both the source facts behind the draft and the report showing what the simulated reader understood, where they stopped, and what they doubted.
emails.objection: An AI assessment of an AI-written email does not prove how real recipients will respond.
must_not_say: Do not call the cold reader a human reviewer or imply that it represents actual customers.
Do not present its assessment as measured opens, clicks, sales, conversions, or proof the email will perform.
Do not guarantee that every draft claim is correct merely because source facts are inspectable.
Do not add a second CTA asking for a reply, meeting, signup, purchase, or public registration.
Do not repeat the setup argument from email 1 or introduce pricing, testimonials, sending features, competitor research, LinkedIn, or the older orqAgent agent builder.
emails.felt_need: I need to know which parts of this draft are grounded in my material and where an unfamiliar reader may lose the thread before I decide what belongs in the campaign.
emails.mechanism: On the Knowledge page, the reader can inspect compiled facts, supporting quotations, evidence identifiers, strength labels, and missing information. emails.call_to_action: Sign in to your existing MarketingOS workspace, open the completed campaign, and inspect its Knowledge page and “Why it scored what it scored” report before deciding what you would keep or rewrite.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide which language is usable, which claims need checking, and which parts of the draft should be rewritten before it goes anywhere else.
emails.next_step_value: The account exposes the compiled facts and supporting material alongside a specific diagnosis of what the simulated reader understood, where they stopped, and their biggest doubt.
emails.next_step_limit: This review helps assess the draft itself; it does not establish how real recipients will open, click, buy, or otherwise respond.

events.body:
Use MarketingOS to request one launch or onboarding email for a real SaaS offer. That is enough to put your existing account to a useful test.

Register the brand in your workspace, add the offer’s real source material, and request a single email. MarketingOS reads that material into compiled facts the draft is allowed to claim before writing.

You get something concrete to judge without committing to a full sequence: one draft grounded in the material you supplied. It is still a draft, not an approval—check its facts, links, and brand voice before copying anything into your sending tool.

The result lets you decide whether the draft is worth reviewing further for this campaign.

events.body:
MarketingOS starts with the material behind one real offer. It reads that material into compiled facts it is allowed to claim, then uses those facts to draft the launch or onboarding email you request.

You do not need to begin with a full sequence. Register your brand in your existing workspace, add the website material or pasted text for one offer, and request one email.

That gives you a bounded test: a concrete draft built from the offer material you supplied, so you can decide whether it is worth reviewing further for this campaign.

MarketingOS does not replace your approval. Check the draft’s facts, links, and brand voice before copying any of it into your sending tool.

Only these audience facts are established. Do not substitute a compiled market segment, invent an installed tool or experience, or infer the campaign's desired reaction. Read the email cold as this person.
readers.what_it_sells: MarketingOS is an application that researches and drafts launch or onboarding emails, then shows the evidence behind the draft and a simulated-reader report to help me revise it.
readers.biggest_doubt: I cannot tell whether there is anything ready for me to inspect or whether clicking will begin a longer setup task that I do not have time for before my meeting.
readers.stopped_at: Your MarketingOS workspace may not contain a completed campaign yet.
fixes: Rewrite "Your MarketingOS workspace may not contain a completed campaign yet. If it does not, add material for one real SaaS offer and generate a launch or onboarding email; the review becomes available with the completed campaign." to state whether my review is ready; if the sender cannot know, separate the quick inspection path from the campaign-creation path and state the expected effort.
Cut or shorten "MarketingOS is an email campaign drafting and market-research application." because an invited account holder needs the immediate reason to return before a general product definition.

Rewrite "Sign in, open a completed campaign, and use both views to decide which language to keep, which claims need checking, and what to rewrite." to say how long the inspection takes and what I will see first after clicking.
Rewrite "Open your MarketingOS workspace →" to distinguish "View your campaign review" from "Create a campaign" so the click does not conceal two different levels of effort.

events.message:
Request: Write exactly two English emails introducing MarketingOS to invited early-access testers who already have a test account. They run a small SaaS business and need to write a launch or onboarding email campaign. Explain one concrete supported reason to try the product, then invite them to test one real offer and review the output. Do not assume their present tools, revenue, list size, staffing, email results or urgency. Do not invent prices, testimonials, performance gains or public signup. Make the first action small: sign in, add the real offer material, and request one email. In the second email explain why inspecting source facts and reader feedback is useful. One clear CTA in each email to their existing account. The product is MarketingOS, not the older orqAgent AI agent builder.
Delivered 2 of 2 email(s). Average AI simulation assessment (uncalibrated) 8.0/10.
- Email 1 "Would you put one MarketingOS draft under your name?": The smallest useful MarketingOS test is one email for a real offer, because the product first turns the supplied material into a set of facts the draft is allowed to use. - pull 8/10 after 1 rewrite(s) - and argues from none of the evidence it was assigned
- Email 2 "What can you use from the draft?": The useful review is not a score taken on faith: the reader can inspect both the source facts behind the draft and the report showing what the simulated reader understood, where they stopped, and what they doubted. - unresolved audience mismatch (AI simulation) after 2 rewrite(s)
Email(s) 2 did not satisfy the simulated assessment criteria. The loop stopped rewriting them; it did not decide these were ready to send.
Unresolved before sending: Email 2: Unresolved audience mismatch: The profile-supported need for launch or onboarding email copy makes the general product relevant, and the existing account is also established. However, the immediate CTA assumes a specific completed campaign and two populated views are already waiting; that is an email-only premise, not established by the profile, so I cannot tell whether there is anything useful for me to inspect now.
Sequence: The sequence has a coherent create-then-review arc, but Email 2 depends on an unverified action from Email 1.
Email(s) 1: the automatic check did not match the copy to its assigned evidence. Review its claims against the sources; this check can miss paraphrases and does not establish whether a claim is true or invented.
What held the copy back: No price or free-entry terms found - emails cannot name a price, a trial length or a risk reversal; No customer names, quotes or case studies found - the copy can describe the product but cannot prove anyone uses it; No measurable results found - claims stay qualitative, and adjectives convert worse than numbers
What would help most next time: Recheck the selected audience situation: The profile-supported need for launch or onboarding email copy makes the general product relevant, and the existing account is also established. However, the immediate CTA assumes a specific completed campaign and two populated views are already waiting; that is an email-only premise, not established by the profile, so I cannot tell whether there is anything useful for me to inspect now.
